---
title: "Private Cloud & On-Premises"
description: "Run PipesHub on your own hardware, including air-gapped networks"
icon: "building"
---

PipesHub is designed to run entirely inside your own network. Nothing about the core product requires an outbound connection once the images are on the host, which makes it suitable for regulated environments and air-gapped networks.

## Requirements

- A Linux host with Docker and Compose 2.20 or later.
- 4 CPU cores and a 16 GB-class machine. The installer stops below 4 cores, and warns below 16 GB of RAM or 20 GB of free disk. Leave more disk for your indexed content. See [System Requirements](/deployment/system-requirements).
- Internal DNS pointing a hostname at the machine.
- A TLS certificate, from your internal certificate authority or a public one.

## Install

The [Deployment Overview](/deployment/overview) covers the standard install. On a machine with internet access:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install | bash
```

## Air-gapped installation

On a host with no internet access, use the `full` deployment type. Its image tag, `latest`, has the embedding model built in; the `slim` image downloads the model on first use and cannot do that offline. The `full` type uses Kafka as its message broker.

**On a machine that does have access,** download the deployment files for a release and save the images:

```bash
REF=v1.0.0   # the release you want
mkdir pipeshub && cd pipeshub
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/$REF/deployment/docker-compose/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai/$REF/deployment/docker-compose/install.sh
chmod +x install.sh

docker pull pipeshubai/pipeshub-ai:latest
docker pull pipeshubai/pipeshub-sandbox:latest
docker pull mongo:8.0.17
docker pull redis:7.4-bookworm
docker pull qdrant/qdrant:v1.15
docker pull neo4j:5.26.0
docker pull confluentinc/cp-zookeeper:7.9.0
docker pull confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.9.0

docker save -o pipeshub-images.tar \
  pipeshubai/pipeshub-ai:latest pipeshubai/pipeshub-sandbox:latest \
  mongo:8.0.17 redis:7.4-bookworm qdrant/qdrant:v1.15 neo4j:5.26.0 \
  confluentinc/cp-zookeeper:7.9.0 confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.9.0
```

These image versions are the ones in the Compose file for that release; check `docker-compose.yml` if you use a different one. If you choose ArangoDB instead of Neo4j, save `arangodb:3.12.4`; for etcd as the key-value store, save `quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.17`.

The sandbox image is only needed if agents should run code. To leave it out, install the `eval` type with the `latest` image (`PIPESHUB_DEPLOY_TYPE=eval ./install.sh --version latest --no-pull`). `eval` uses Redis instead of Kafka, so you can also skip the two Kafka images, but agents cannot run code.

**On the air-gapped host,** copy the `pipeshub` directory and `pipeshub-images.tar` across, then load the images and install without pulling:

```bash
docker load -i pipeshub-images.tar
cd pipeshub
PIPESHUB_DEPLOY_TYPE=full ./install.sh --version latest --no-pull
```

`--no-pull` tells the installer to use the images already present. `--version` must match the tag you saved; otherwise the installer looks for an image you do not have.

After the install, set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1` in `.env` and run `docker compose -p pipeshub-ai up -d`, so the model libraries do not try to reach the internet. See [Environment Variables](/deployment/environment-variables#air-gapped-hosts).

## Choosing models

An air-gapped deployment cannot reach a hosted model provider, so configure local ones:

- **Text generation:** [Ollama](/ai-models/llm/ollama) or [vLLM](/ai-models/llm/vllm) on your own hardware.
- **Embeddings:** [Sentence Transformers](/ai-models/embedding/sentence-transformer), which run inside the PipesHub container. The `latest` image includes the default embedding model.
- **Speech to text:** [Whisper](/ai-models/stt/whisper), which runs locally.

Download the weights for your text-generation models on a connected machine before you move them across.

## Telemetry

PipesHub collects usage telemetry by default. On an isolated network those requests simply fail and nothing breaks, but you can turn the collection off so the attempts stop: switch off **Data collection settings** under **Workspace → General**, or set `TELEMETRY_COLLECTION_FLAG=false` in `.env`.

## Certificates

If you terminate TLS with a certificate from an internal certificate authority, make sure that authority is trusted by the machines people browse from. PipesHub itself does not care which authority signed it.

## Day-two operations

```bash
./install.sh --stop         # stop, keeping data
./install.sh --upgrade      # recreate containers using the current images
./install.sh --uninstall    # stop and delete all data
```

On an air-gapped host, `--upgrade` will not find new images. Load the new images with `docker load` first, then run `./install.sh --upgrade --no-pull`. Before upgrading from 0.x, read [Upgrading to 1.0](/deployment/upgrade-to-1-0).

For backup and restore, see [Backup and Restore](/deployment/backup-restore).
